{{refimprove|date=December 2009}}
Suppose that <math>(\mathcal C,\otimes,I)</math> and <math>(\mathcal D,\bullet, J)</math> are two [[monoidal category|monoidal categories]] and
:<math>(F,m):(\mathcal C,\otimes,I)\to(\mathcal D,\bullet, J)</math> and <math>(G,n):(\mathcal C,\otimes,I)\to(\mathcal D,\bullet, J)</math>
are two [[lax monoidal functor]]s between those categories.

A '''monoidal natural transformation'''
:<math>\theta:(F,m) \to (G,n)</math>
between those functors is a [[natural transformation]] <math>\theta:F \to G</math> between the underlying functors such that the diagrams
:[[File:Monoidal natural transformation multiplication.svg]] {{spaces|10}} and {{spaces|8}} [[File:Monoidal natural transformation unit.svg]]
commute for every objects <math>A</math> and <math>B</math> of <math>\mathcal C</math>.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Baez|first1=John C.|author-link1=John C. Baez|title=Some Definitions Everyone Should Know|url=http://math.ucr.edu/home/baez/qg-fall2004/definitions.pdf|accessdate=2 December 2014}}</ref><ref>{{harvp|Perrone|2024|page=369}}</ref>

A '''symmetric monoidal natural transformation''' is a monoidal natural transformation between [[symmetric monoidal functor]]s.
